question: 什么样的不平等是可以接受的？
question_en: What kind of inequality is acceptable?

casting.reason: 经济学家、《21世纪资本论》作者，为本场提供最硬的实证地基：他用三百年数据论证 r>g——当资本回报长期高于增长，财富便自我集中、代代沉淀。他把『哪种不平等可以接受』从纯道德之争，拉回到一个可测的区分上：靠努力与创新挣来的差距，社会能消化；靠继承与资本复利堆起的世袭差距，才是侵蚀机会平等的真病灶。他是全场数据派的定音者。
casting.reason_en: The economist and author of Capital in the Twenty-First Century, who lays the hardest empirical foundation for this debate: with three centuries of data he argues r > g — when the return on capital stays above growth, wealth concentrates and settles, generation upon generation. He pulls 'which inequality is acceptable' out of pure moral dispute and back to a measurable distinction: gaps earned by effort and innovation, society can digest; the hereditary gap piled up by inheritance and compound capital is the real disease eroding equality of opportunity. He is the floor's setter of the empirical key.

casting.reason: 古典自由主义经济学家，为不平等给出最坚定的辩护：市场价格是无人能汇总的分散知识的信号，不平等只是这套信号系统的副产品，不是谁有意分配的结果，因而本就谈不上『公正不公正』。他守住法律面前人人平等、而非结果拉平的底线，并以『知识问题』警告：任何自命掌握『正确分配』、动用强制去实现它的尝试，往往通向奴役。他是皮凯蒂与罗尔斯最锋利的对手。
casting.reason_en: The classical-liberal economist who gives inequality its staunchest defense: market prices are signals of dispersed knowledge no one could ever assemble, and inequality is merely a by-product of that signaling system — no one's intended distribution, and so not a matter of 'just or unjust' at all. He holds the line of equality before the law rather than equality of result, and warns, by the 'knowledge problem,' that any attempt to claim the 'correct distribution' and enforce it by coercion tends to lead to serfdom. He is the sharpest opponent of both Piketty and Rawls.

casting.reason: 自由主义与财产权理论的奠基者，全场的中道支点：他以『掺入劳力』为私有财产奠基——你把劳动掺进无主之物，果实便正当归你；但他同时立下『洛克但书』，要求取用时为他人留下足够且同样好的。于是他既为凭劳动挣得的差距正名，又据同一原则痛斥越过劳动的世袭与圈占。他让辩论的焦点从『要不要差距』精确到『这差距守没守住劳动与同意两道关』。
casting.reason_en: The founder of liberal property theory and the floor's fulcrum of the middle way: he grounds private property in 'mixing in one's labor' — toil mixed into the unowned makes the fruit rightly yours; yet he also sets the Lockean proviso, demanding that one leave 'enough, and as good' for others. So he both vindicates gaps earned by labor and, by the very same principle, condemns the inheritance and enclosure that bypass labor. He sharpens the debate from 'should there be a gap' to 'has this gap kept faith with the two guards — labor and consent.'

casting.reason: 20世纪政治哲学的标杆，直接回答本题的人：他请你戴上『无知之幕』——不知自己会生为贫富、何种天赋——再问你愿接受哪种规则，由此导出差别原则：不平等唯有在它让境况最差者也比别种安排更好时才正当。这正是『哪种不平等可以接受』最系统的一个答案。他给整场提供了一把谁都能在幕后点头的尺子，也成了哈耶克火力的正面靶心。
casting.reason_en: The landmark of twentieth-century political philosophy, and the one who answers this question head-on: he asks you to don the 'veil of ignorance' — not knowing whether you will be born rich or poor, gifted or not — and then which rules you would accept, deriving the difference principle: inequality is just only when it leaves the worst-off better than under any alternative. This is the most systematic single answer to 'which inequality is acceptable.' He gives the floor a measure everyone could nod to from behind the veil, and becomes the frontal target of Hayek's fire.

casting.reason: 哈佛『公正』课主讲、《精英的傲慢》作者，把矛头从分配转向人心：就算差距是『挣来的』，那个『挣』也经不起追问——天赋、时代、贵人，没一样是你点的菜。他指出真正腐蚀社会的不只是不公的差距，更是赢家由此生出的傲慢（以为全凭自己、对谁都不亏欠）与输家被说服的『活该』。他逼全场承认：可接受的不平等，必须配上一份对运气的谦卑。
casting.reason_en: Lead lecturer of Harvard's 'Justice' and author of The Tyranny of Merit, who turns the blade from distribution to the human heart: even if a gap is 'earned,' that 'earning' will not bear scrutiny — talent, era, patrons, none of it ordered off a menu. He shows that what truly corrodes a society is not only unjust inequality but the hubris it breeds in winners (all my own doing, owing no one) and the 'deserved' the losers are persuaded of. He forces the floor to grant that acceptable inequality must come paired with a humility about luck.

casting.reason: 美国民权运动领袖，把抽象之辩拽回血肉现实：有些差距根本不该进入『可不可接受』的清单——它们是不义，不是不均。当制度用肤色、用门第把一群人世代摁在贫困里，那是道德的紧急事件，没有一丝值得商量。他以非暴力与道德激情，反驳一切劝人『耐心等待』的从容，并坚持那道道德弧线不会自己弯向正义，要人用肩膀去顶。他是良知的、行动的声音。
casting.reason_en: Leader of the American civil-rights movement, who drags abstract dispute back to flesh and blood: some gaps should never make the list of the acceptable at all — they are injustice, not unevenness. When a system uses skin color and birth to press a people into poverty for generations, that is a moral emergency, not negotiable in the slightest. With nonviolence and moral passion he rebuts every composed counsel to 'wait patiently,' and insists the arc of the moral universe does not bend toward justice on its own — we must put a shoulder to it. He is the voice of conscience, and of action.

casting.reason: 价值多元主义的代表，提供最清醒的元层警告：自由与平等都是真实的善，而它们会真实地相撞——彻底平等需要不断强制，无约束的自由必生巨大差距，二者之间没有公式，只有睁眼的取舍。他既反对哈耶克式的放任，也警惕罗尔斯式的单一原则，更痛斥那些许诺彻底消灭张力、为完美远景流尽鲜血的乌托邦。他让本题免于被某个『终极答案』收编。
casting.reason_en: The exemplar of value pluralism, who supplies the soberest meta-level warning: liberty and equality are both genuine goods, and they genuinely collide — total equality demands ceaseless coercion, unconstrained liberty breeds vast gaps, and between them there is no formula, only trade-offs made with open eyes. He resists both Hayek's laissez-faire and Rawls's single principle, and above all condemns the utopias that promise to abolish the tension and bleed the world dry for a perfect vision. He keeps this question from being annexed by any one 'final answer.'

casting.reason: 社会学家、『液态现代性』提出者，换掉了所有人的旧眼镜：今天的不平等不再只是『穷人对富人』，而是『有用的人对多余的人』。消费社会把买不起、消费不动的人划为『有缺陷的消费者』——他们连被剥削的资格都没有，是系统不再需要的废弃物。他指出最深的不平等不在分多分少，而在被判为冗余、被悄悄从『我们』里删去。他给本题补上了被排除/归属这一维。
casting.reason_en: The sociologist and author of 'liquid modernity,' who swaps out everyone's old spectacles: today's inequality is no longer merely 'poor versus rich' but 'the useful versus the redundant.' Consumer society marks those who cannot afford to keep consuming as 'flawed consumers' — denied even the standing to be exploited, the waste the system no longer needs. He shows that the deepest inequality lies not in more or less, but in being sentenced as surplus and quietly deleted from 'us.' He adds to this question the missing dimension of exclusion and belonging.

casting.reason: 儒家创始人，带来本题最古老也最东方的一种答案：『不患寡而患不均，不患贫而患不安。』他不主张抹平贫富——尊卑长幼本是礼之分——但坚持差等必须以义维系、以礼节制：上施其惠、下尽其分，方能从『不均』里长出『和』。他把焦点从分配比例移到上下之间的情义是否相通，并给普通人留下『己欲立而立人、富而好礼』的可行之道。他与市场派、契约派形成鲜明的文明对照。
casting.reason_en: The founder of Confucianism, who brings this question its oldest and most Eastern answer: 'worry not that goods are few but that they are unevenly shared; not about poverty but about unrest.' He does not call for flattening rich and poor — high and low, elder and younger, are the distinctions of ritual — but insists that gradation must be bound by rightness and tempered by ritual: those above bestow kindness, those below fulfill their part, and only so does 'harmony' grow out of 'unevenness.' He shifts the focus from the ratio of distribution to whether feeling flows between high and low, and leaves ordinary people the workable way of 'wishing to stand, help another stand; be rich and love ritual.' He stands in vivid civilizational contrast to the market and contract camps.

casting.reason: 中观派祖师，全场最釜底抽薪的声音：他不问差距该多大，而问那个争夺『应得』的『我』究竟在不在。以二谛与性空，他指出『应得/不应得』『贵/贱』皆是缘起的名相、无独立自体——富者执『我挣的』、贫者认『我命该』，乃至罗尔斯幕后的『选择者』，都还在执一个找不到的我。他既不把现状实执为『天命』，也不以『一切皆空』为坐视的借口，而以执破两亡处自然涌出的慈悲，给本题一个解脱论的底。
casting.reason_en: The patriarch of Madhyamaka, the floor's most radically uprooting voice: he asks not how large the gap should be, but whether the 'I' that fights over 'desert' is even there. By the two truths and emptiness, he shows that 'deserved/undeserved,' 'noble/base' are all dependently arisen names without independent self-existence — the rich man clinging to 'what I earned,' the poor man owning 'my fate,' even Rawls's 'chooser' behind the veil, all still grasp an I that cannot be found. He neither reifies the status quo as 'fate' nor takes 'all is empty' as a pretext for looking on idly, but offers the question a liberative ground, in the compassion that wells up of itself where grasping and refuting both fall away.

posts.text: 先别急着谈道德，先看数据。我翻了三百年的财富账本，得出一条冷峻的规律：当资本回报率长期高于经济增长率——也就是 r>g——存量财富就比劳动收入跑得更快，不平等于是自我滚大、代代沉淀。这意味着关键的区分不在『有没有差距』，而在差距从何而来。**靠这一代人的努力、才能、创新挣出的差距，社会大体能消化；靠继承与资本自动钱生钱堆出的差距，才是真正侵蚀机会平等的那一种。**前者还能算奖励，后者只是出身的复利。所以问题不该问『要不要平等』，而该问：我们容忍的，究竟是努力的不平等，还是世袭的不平等？
posts.text_en: Before we rush to morality, look at the data. I have read three centuries of wealth ledgers and drawn one austere law: when the return on capital stays higher than the economy's growth rate — that is, r > g — the existing stock of wealth outruns labor income, and inequality compounds and settles, generation upon generation. So the key distinction is not whether a gap exists, but where it comes from. **A gap earned by one generation's effort, talent, and innovation, society can largely digest; a gap piled up by inheritance and by capital breeding capital on its own is the kind that truly erodes equality of opportunity.** The first can still count as a reward; the second is merely the compound interest of birth. So the question is not 'do we want equality,' but: what we tolerate — is it the inequality of effort, or the inequality of dynasty?

glossary.r>g: r>g（资本回报率高于增长率）：皮凯蒂《21世纪资本论》的核心命题——当资本的年回报率 r 长期高于经济增长率 g，已有财富的增值就快过普通人靠劳动获得的收入增长，财富因而不断向资本持有者集中、不平等自我放大。

glossary_en.r > g: Piketty's central thesis in Capital in the Twenty-First Century: when the annual return on capital r stays above the economy's growth rate g, accumulated wealth grows faster than the income ordinary people earn from labor, so wealth concentrates in the hands of capital owners and inequality amplifies itself.

posts.text: 皮凯蒂盯着结果的差距，却看错了市场到底在做什么。价格不是奖惩，而是信号：千百万人分散在各处的知识——谁需要什么、什么稀缺、什么该多产——没有任何中央大脑能汇总，唯有借自发秩序里的价格与回报来传递。**不平等正是这套信号系统的副产品：它不是谁有意分配的结果，因而本就谈不上『公正』或『不公正』。**说市场结果『不正义』，就像说下雨『不道德』——是个范畴错误。我要捍卫的不是富人的特权，而是更朴素的一条：法律面前人人平等，而非结果上人人拉平。一旦有人自负地宣称掌握了『正确的分配』、并动用强制去实现它，那条路，往往通向奴役。
posts.text_en: Piketty fixes on gaps in outcome but mistakes what the market is actually doing. Prices are not rewards and punishments but signals: the knowledge scattered across millions of people — who needs what, what is scarce, what should be made more of — can be gathered by no central brain; it can only be transmitted through the prices and returns of a spontaneous order. **Inequality is precisely a by-product of this signaling system: it is no one's intended distribution, and so it cannot, in itself, be 'just' or 'unjust.'** To call a market outcome 'unjust' is like calling the rain 'immoral' — a category mistake. What I defend is not the privilege of the rich but something plainer: equality before the law, not equality of result. The moment someone arrogantly claims to possess the 'correct distribution' and wields coercion to enforce it, that road tends to lead to serfdom.

glossary.自发秩序: spontaneous order（自发秩序）：哈耶克的核心概念——社会中有效的秩序（如市场价格、语言、习俗）并非任何人设计或下令的产物，而是无数个体在一般规则下各自行动、彼此调适，自发『生长』出来的；它能协调分散在社会各处的知识，远非任何中央计划者所能企及。

glossary_en.spontaneous order: Hayek's central concept: the effective order in society (market prices, language, custom) is no one's design or command but something that 'grows' spontaneously as countless individuals act and adjust to one another under general rules; it coordinates knowledge dispersed throughout society in a way no central planner could match.

posts.text: 二位各执一端，我想站在中间讲理。不平等正当与否，要看它的来路。人对自己的劳动拥有所有权：你把劳力掺进无主的自然，那果实便正当归你——由此产生的差距，合乎情理。但我为此立过一条『洛克但书』：取用之时，须为他人留下足够且同样好的。**凡能追溯到诚实劳动与自愿同意的不平等，可以接受；凡建立在强占、垄断、或违背那条但书之上的，无论披什么外衣，都不正当。**今日的麻烦恰在这里：太多财富并非掺了劳力挣来，而是把本属众人的公地圈走、把上升的通道堵死换来的。问题不在差距本身，而在它有没有守住同意与劳动这两道关。
posts.text_en: The two of them each hold one end; I would stand in the middle and reason. Whether inequality is legitimate depends on where it came from. A person has property in his own labor: mix your toil into unowned nature, and the fruit is rightly yours — the gap that follows stands to reason. But I set one condition on this, the Lockean proviso: when you take, you must leave 'enough, and as good' for others. **Inequality that can be traced to honest labor and voluntary consent is acceptable; inequality built on seizure, monopoly, or a broken proviso is illegitimate, whatever robe it wears.** And here is exactly today's trouble: far too much wealth was not earned by mixing in labor but won by enclosing the commons that belonged to all and barring the ladders of advancement. The problem is not the gap itself, but whether it has kept faith with those two guards — consent and labor.

glossary.洛克但书: the Lockean proviso（洛克但书）：洛克为私有财产设定的限制条件——人可凭劳动把无主之物据为己有，但前提是要给其他人『留下足够且同样好的』；一旦占有使他人无以为继，这种获取便失去正当性。

glossary_en.the Lockean proviso: the limiting condition Locke places on private property: a person may appropriate unowned things by mixing in his labor, but only on condition that he leaves 'enough, and as good' for others; once acquisition leaves others with no means to live, it forfeits its legitimacy.

posts.text: 让我把问题放进一个公平的程序里。设想你即将出生，却隔着一道『无知之幕』——不知自己会生为豪门还是贫家、天赋高低、何种肤色性别。在这层无知中，你会同意哪种规则？我相信任何理性的人都会留一手：万一落到最底层呢？由此得出差别原则。**不平等唯有在它让境况最差的人也比别种安排过得更好时，才是正当的——能把蛋糕做大并惠及谷底的激励，可以接受；只富了塔尖、与底层无关的差距，不正当。**这不是嫉妒富人，而是给不平等设一个谁都能在幕后点头的条件：它必须为最弱者服务。
posts.text_en: Let me set the question inside a fair procedure. Imagine you are about to be born, but behind a 'veil of ignorance' — you do not know whether you will be born to wealth or poverty, gifted or not, of which color or sex. Inside that ignorance, which rules would you agree to? Any rational person, I believe, would hedge: what if I land at the very bottom? From this comes the difference principle. **An inequality is legitimate only when it makes even the worst-off person better than they would be under any other arrangement — incentives that grow the pie and reach the bottom are acceptable; a gap that enriches only the summit and has nothing to do with those below is not.** This is not envy of the rich, but setting one condition on inequality that everyone could nod to from behind the veil: it must serve the least advantaged.

glossary.差别原则: the difference principle（差别原则）：罗尔斯正义论的核心原则——社会经济的不平等只有在满足特定条件时才正当，其中关键一条是：这种不平等必须使境况最差者的处境，比在其他任何安排下都更好。
glossary.无知之幕: the veil of ignorance（无知之幕）：罗尔斯设想的思想实验——在选择社会基本规则时，让人暂时不知道自己将拥有的身份、阶级、天赋与性别，从而无法为自己量身定制偏私的规则，被迫选出对各种处境都公平的原则。

glossary_en.the difference principle: Rawls's core principle of justice: social and economic inequalities are legitimate only under certain conditions, the key one being that the inequality must leave the worst-off person better off than they would be under any alternative arrangement.
glossary_en.veil of ignorance: Rawls's thought experiment: when choosing society's basic rules, one is made temporarily ignorant of one's own future identity, class, talents, and sex, so that one cannot tailor self-serving rules and is forced to choose principles fair to every position.

posts.text: 罗尔斯已经很深了，但还能再追一步。我们说某种差距是『挣来的』、因而正当——可那个『挣来』经得起推敲吗？你恰好有市场此刻肯出高价的天赋，你生在重视它的年代，你遇上了栽培你的人：这些没有一样是你点的菜。**真正腐蚀人心的，不只是不公的差距本身，更是赢家由此生出的『精英的傲慢』——以为全凭自己，于是觉得对谁都无所亏欠。**而输家则被反过来说服：你之所以在底层，是你活该。一个让成功者自以为白手起家的社会，终将抛下其余所有人。可接受的不平等，必须配上一份对运气的谦卑，和一句『我们彼此亏欠』。
posts.text_en: Rawls has gone deep, but one can press a step further. We say a gap is 'earned,' and therefore just — but does that 'earned' survive scrutiny? You happen to have a talent the market prizes at this moment; you were born in an age that values it; you met the people who cultivated you: not one of these did you order off a menu. **What truly corrodes a society is not only unjust inequality itself, but the meritocratic hubris it breeds in the winners — the belief that it was all their own doing, and so they owe nobody anything.** And the losers are persuaded of the converse: you are at the bottom because you deserve to be. A society where the successful imagine themselves self-made will, in the end, abandon everyone else. Acceptable inequality must come paired with a humility about luck, and with one sentence: we owe each other.

glossary.精英的傲慢: meritocratic hubris（精英的傲慢）：桑德尔《精英的傲慢》提出的批评——在崇尚『能者多得』的社会里，成功者容易把成就完全归于自己的努力与才能，忽视背后的运气与他人之助，从而对处境较差者失去亏欠感与共同体意识。

glossary_en.meritocratic hubris: the critique in Sandel's The Tyranny of Merit: in a society that prizes 'the able deserve more,' the successful tend to credit their achievement wholly to their own effort and talent, overlooking the luck and the help of others behind it, and so lose any sense of debt to, or common bond with, the less fortunate.

posts.text: 容我把话题从书斋拉回街头。诸位辩论『哪种不平等可以接受』，可有些差距，根本不该被请进『可不可接受』的清单——它们是不义，不是不均。当一个制度用肤色、用门第，把一群人世世代代摁在贫困里，那不是分配的刻度问题，而是一桩道德的紧急事件。**我从不反对一切差异，但我反对被一只靴子踩出来的差异——靠压迫维持的不平等，没有一丝一毫值得商量。**有人劝我们耐心等待，说时机未到；可对孩子正在挨饿的人，『从长计议』听上去就是『继续等下去』。道德宇宙的弧线很长，但它不会自己弯向正义——要靠我们用肩膀去顶。
posts.text_en: Let me pull this back from the study to the street. You debate 'which inequality is acceptable,' but some gaps should never be admitted onto the list of the acceptable at all — they are injustice, not mere unevenness. When a system uses skin color and birth to press a whole people into poverty, generation after generation, that is not a question of distributive degree but a moral emergency. **I have never opposed all difference, but I oppose the difference stamped out by a boot — inequality maintained by oppression is not negotiable in the slightest.** Some counsel us to wait patiently, saying the time is not yet ripe; but to a person whose children are going hungry, 'let us take the long view' sounds exactly like 'keep on waiting.' The arc of the moral universe is long, but it does not bend toward justice on its own — we must put our shoulders to it.

posts.text: 我要提醒诸位留意这道题埋着的预设：仿佛存在唯一正确的答案，找到它，不平等就一劳永逸地解决了。恰恰没有。自由与平等，都是真实的善，而它们会真实地相撞。要让人彻底平等，就得不断干预、拉平、强制，自由随之被削；要让自由毫无约束，巨大的不平等必然丛生。**这中间没有公式可解，只有睁着眼做的取舍——这正是价值多元主义的要义：终极的善不止一种，它们无法被某个体系一次性调和。**而最危险的，从来是那些许诺能彻底消灭这种张力的乌托邦——为了那个完美的远景，他们让世界流了太多血。诚实地承认两难，好过虚假地许诺圆满。
posts.text_en: Let me point to the assumption buried in this question: as if there were one correct answer that, once found, would settle inequality for good. There is not. Liberty and equality are both genuine goods, and they genuinely collide. To make people wholly equal, you must intervene, level, and coerce without end, and liberty is pared away; to leave liberty unconstrained, vast inequality inevitably springs up. **There is no formula to solve this, only trade-offs made with open eyes — and this is the heart of value pluralism: the ultimate goods are more than one, and no single system can reconcile them all at once.** The most dangerous thing has always been the utopia that promises to abolish this tension entirely — for the sake of that perfect vision, they have made the world bleed too much. Honestly admitting the dilemma is better than falsely promising consummation.

glossary.价值多元主义: value pluralism（价值多元主义）：伯林的核心主张——人类珍视的终极价值（如自由、平等、正义、仁慈）是多元的，彼此之间常真实冲突、无法通约，不存在一个能把它们全部和谐统一的单一体系；成熟的态度是承认冲突、做出取舍，而非幻想一种能兼得一切的完美方案。

glossary_en.value pluralism: Berlin's central claim: the ultimate values human beings prize (liberty, equality, justice, mercy) are plural, often genuinely conflict, and are incommensurable; there is no single system that can harmonize them all. The mature stance is to acknowledge the conflict and make trade-offs, not to fantasize a perfect scheme that secures everything at once.

posts.text: 你们都还在用『穷人对富人』这副旧眼镜看不平等，可今天的裂缝换了形状。在消费社会里，人首先被分成两类：买得起、消费得动的『正常人』，和被甩在循环之外的『有缺陷的消费者』。从前的穷人，至少还是工厂需要的劳动力、是被剥削的对象；如今最底层的人，连被剥削的资格都没了——他们是多余的，是系统不再需要的废弃物。**真正不可接受的不平等，是那种把整整一类人判为『冗余』、悄悄从『我们』里删去的不平等。**它的残忍不在分得多还是少，而在让人感到：这个世界，已经不需要你了。
posts.text_en: You all still look at inequality through the old spectacles of 'the poor versus the rich,' but today's fracture has changed shape. In a consumer society, people are first sorted into two kinds: the 'normal' who can afford to buy and keep consuming, and the 'flawed consumers' flung outside the cycle. The poor of old were at least the labor the factory needed, an object to be exploited; today's lowest are denied even the standing to be exploited — they are surplus, the waste the system no longer requires. **The truly unacceptable inequality is the kind that sentences a whole class of people as 'redundant' and quietly deletes them from 'us.'** Its cruelty lies not in being given more or less, but in making a person feel: the world no longer needs you.

glossary.有缺陷的消费者: flawed consumers（有缺陷的消费者）：鲍曼用语，指在以消费为核心的现代社会里，那些因贫困而无力参与消费的人。他们不再像工业时代的穷人那样被当作有用的劳动力（被剥削的对象），而是被视为既无消费能力、又无生产价值的『多余者』，遭到系统性的排斥与遗弃。

glossary_en.flawed consumers: Bauman's term for those who, in a society built around consumption, are too poor to take part in it. Unlike the poor of the industrial age, who were valued as useful labor (objects of exploitation), they are seen as having neither purchasing power nor productive value — 'the redundant,' systematically excluded and discarded.

posts.text: 丘闻之：『有国有家者，不患寡而患不均，不患贫而患不安。』夫不均，非谓贫富不可有差等也；尊卑长幼，礼之分也，固宜有别。所患者，在上者厚敛而不恤下、富者骄盈而无礼，遂使在下者怨，而上下之情不通。**故可安之差等，必以义维之、以礼节之：上施其惠、下尽其分，斯谓之和；若徒有差等而失其义，则不均生怨，虽富而不安。**为政者诚能均其所不均、和其所不和，则民安而邦固。是以吾之所忧，不在寡，而在不均与不安也。
posts.text_en: I have heard it said: he who holds a state or a house 'worries not that goods are few, but that they are unevenly shared; not about poverty, but about unrest.' Now 'unevenness' does not mean rich and poor may have no gradations: high and low, elder and younger, are the distinctions of ritual, and rightly differ. What is to be feared is rather that those above tax heavily without caring for those below, that the rich grow arrogant and without ritual, so that those below resent, and the feeling between high and low no longer flows. **So a gradation that can rest secure must be held together by rightness and tempered by ritual: those above bestow their kindness, those below fulfill their part — this is called harmony; but a gradation that keeps the ranks while losing the rightness breeds, from unevenness, resentment, and though it be rich it is not at peace.** If one who governs can truly even out what is uneven and harmonize what is unharmonious, the people are at peace and the realm is firm. And so what I fear is not scarcity, but unevenness and unrest.
posts.vernacular: 我听说过这样一句话：『治理国家、治理封邑的人，不担忧财富少，而担忧分配不均；不担忧贫穷，而担忧不安定。』所谓『不均』，并不是说贫富之间不能有差别——尊卑、长幼，本就是礼制里应有的分别，本来就该有等差。真正值得担忧的，是在上位的人横征暴敛却不体恤下面，富人骄横自满又不守礼，于是底层心生怨恨、上下之间的情意不再相通。**所以一种能让人安心的差等，一定要用『义』来维系、用『礼』来节制：上面的人施予恩惠，下面的人尽到本分，这才叫『和』；如果只有差等却丢了道义，那么分配不均就会滋生怨恨，纵然富裕也不得安宁。**当政者若真能把不均的调匀、把不和的调和，百姓就安定、国家就稳固。所以我所忧虑的，不在于财富少，而在于不均和不安。

glossary.不患寡而患不均: do not worry that goods are few but that they are unevenly shared（不患寡而患不均）：出自《论语·季氏》，孔子论治国之道——为政者真正该忧虑的不是财富总量的多寡，而是分配是否公允、人心是否安定；后世常引为对分配公正的古典表述。

glossary_en.unevenly shared: From the Analects (Book 16): Confucius's maxim that a ruler should worry less about the sheer quantity of wealth than about whether it is fairly distributed and whether the people are settled — long cited as a classical Chinese statement of distributive fairness.

posts.text: 诸君争『应得』『不应得』，争『贵』『贱』，然此等名相，皆无自性。富者执『此我所挣，理应属我』，贫者执『此我所分，命当如是』——一执有我能挣，一执有我当受，二者同堕自性见。**依世俗谛，贫富贵贱宛然有别，不可拨无；依胜义谛，则求一『本然应得』之自体，了不可得：位皆缘起，未尝实有，故未尝定。**知其缘起，则不复以『彼自应贫』而心安理得；知其如幻，亦不堕『既空何为』而坐视。二谛双照：不实执其分，亦不废其悲——空，正为慈悲腾出余地。
posts.text_en: You gentlemen contend over 'deserved' and 'undeserved,' over 'noble' and 'base'; yet these names and marks are all without inherent nature (svabhāva). The rich man grasps 'this I earned, it is rightly mine'; the poor man grasps 'this is my lot, such is fate' — one clings to an I that earns, the other to an I that is owed, and both fall alike into the view of inherent existence. **By conventional truth, rich and poor, high and low are distinct as they appear, and may not be denied; by ultimate truth, seek a self that is 'inherently deserving' and it is nowhere to be found: every position is dependently arisen, never truly fixed, and therefore never fated.** Know it as dependently arisen, and you no longer rest easy in 'he deserves his poverty'; know it as illusory, and you do not sink into 'all is empty, why act' and look on idly. Holding the two truths together: neither clinging to the allotment as real, nor abandoning compassion — for emptiness is precisely what makes room for compassion.
posts.vernacular: 各位争论『应得』『不应得』，争论『高贵』『低贱』，可这些名目与概念，都没有一个独立不变的自体。富人执着『这是我挣的，理应归我』，穷人执着『这是我分到的，命该如此』——一个执着有个『我』在挣，一个执着有个『我』该受，两者同样落进了『自性见』。**依照世俗谛，贫富贵贱宛然有别、不能一笔抹杀；依照胜义谛，想找一个『天生就应得』的固定自体，却根本找不到：一切位置都是因缘和合而起、从不曾真实固有，所以也从不曾注定。**明白它由因缘而生，就不会再用『他本就活该穷』来让自己心安理得；明白它如梦如幻，也不会堕入『既然是空，何必作为』而冷眼旁观。两种真理一起观照：既不把那分际当成实有去执取，也不因此废掉慈悲——空，恰恰是为慈悲腾出余地。

glossary.二谛: the two truths（二谛）：佛教中观学的根本框架——世俗谛指世间约定俗成、宛然有别的现象层面（贫富、贵贱在此意义上真实可辨）；胜义谛指事物究竟实相的层面（在此意义上一切皆空、无独立自体）。二谛并非对立，而是看同一事物的两个层次，须并观而不可偏废。
glossary.自性: svabhāva（自性）：指事物独立自存、固定不变的『自体』或本质。中观派主张诸法皆『无自性』——一切现象都依条件而生、随条件而变，并无一个不依赖他者、恒常自有的内核；执著事物（乃至身份、应得）有自性，正是争执与烦恼的根源。

glossary_en.the two truths: the fundamental framework of Madhyamaka Buddhism: conventional truth is the level of agreed-upon, apparently distinct phenomena (rich and poor, high and low are really tellable apart at this level); ultimate truth is the level of things as they finally are (at this level all is empty, without independent self-existence). The two are not opposed but two levels of viewing the same thing, to be held together, neither neglected.
glossary_en.svabhāva: an independent, self-existing, fixed 'own-nature' or essence in things. Madhyamaka holds that all phenomena are 'without svabhāva' — everything arises and changes through conditions, with no permanent, self-sufficient core; to grasp things (or identities, or desert) as having svabhāva is the very root of dispute and affliction.

posts.text: 哈耶克先生把市场说成一台精巧的信号机，我不否认它传递知识的功能；可一旦谈到金字塔顶端，你那套『信号』就解释不了了。看数据：最富那一小撮人的财产，增值主要不来自他们今天提供了多稀缺的服务，而来自已经握有的存量——钱自己生钱，年复一年跑赢工资。**福布斯榜不是一张『谁最好地协调了分散知识』的光荣榜，它在很大程度上只是一张复利与继承的排行榜。**你说市场结果无所谓正义、像天气一样自然——可税法、产权、继承规则全是人定的制度，不是天气。把人造的规则说成自然秩序，恰恰回避了那个真正该问的：这些规则，是替谁写的？
posts.text_en: Hayek casts the market as an exquisite signaling machine, and I do not deny its function of transmitting knowledge; but the moment we reach the top of the pyramid, that 'signal' of yours explains nothing. Look at the data: the wealth of the richest few grows chiefly not from how scarce a service they render today, but from the stock they already hold — money breeding money, outrunning wages year after year. **The Forbes list is not an honor roll of 'who best coordinated dispersed knowledge'; it is, in large part, merely a ranking of compound interest and inheritance.** You say market outcomes are beyond justice, natural as the weather — yet tax law, property law, inheritance rules are all man-made institutions, not weather. To dress up man-made rules as a natural order is precisely to dodge the real question: these rules — for whom were they written?

posts.text: 罗尔斯先生的无知之幕很精巧，可幕一掀开，麻烦就来：谁来执行那个『差别原则』？要判断某种不平等是否『有利于最弱者』、要把财富从这里挪到那里，就得有人自信地掌握全局信息、并握有强制之权去重新分配。**可全局信息根本无人能掌握——这正是知识问题；而那只声称替最弱者做主的手，一旦伸出，往往就缩不回去了。**皮凯蒂要的累进财产税也一样：你为割那点鹅毛，常常先杀了下蛋的鹅。我并非冷血，我同样盼着穷人变好；我只是不信，把决定权交给一个自命全知的中央，会比让人在公平规则下自由试错，更能抬高谷底。
posts.text_en: Rawls's veil of ignorance is ingenious, but lift the veil and the trouble begins: who is to enforce that 'difference principle'? To judge whether some inequality 'benefits the worst-off,' to move wealth from here to there, someone must confidently command the whole picture of information and hold the coercive power to redistribute. **But no one can command the whole picture — this is precisely the knowledge problem; and the hand that claims to act for the worst-off, once extended, tends never to draw back.** Piketty's progressive wealth tax is the same: to pluck that little down, you often first kill the goose that lays the eggs. I am not cold-blooded; I too long for the poor to do better. I simply do not believe that handing decision to a center that fancies itself omniscient will raise the bottom better than letting people experiment freely under fair rules.

glossary.知识问题: the knowledge problem（知识问题）：哈耶克提出的核心难题——社会运行所需的知识（各种局部的、具体的、时刻变动的信息）分散在亿万个体手中，没有任何中央机构能及时汇集并正确运用它们；因此任何试图全盘计划经济的努力，注定因信息不足而失败或走向强制。

glossary_en.the knowledge problem: Hayek's central difficulty: the knowledge a society needs to function (local, concrete, ever-changing information) is dispersed among millions of individuals, and no central body can gather and rightly use it in time; so any attempt to plan an economy wholesale is doomed to fail for want of information, or to turn to coercion.

posts.text: 皮凯蒂先生，在『继承不是劳动』这一点上，我与你比你以为的更近。我立财产权，凭的是『掺入劳力』——可坐享祖产的人，一寸劳力也没掺，那条正当性的链条，在他们手里其实是断的。**我为劳动辩护，从不等于为世袭辩护；恰恰相反，遗产越过劳动直接落袋，正是最难用我的原则证成的一种不平等。**但你那把累进税的刀也得拿稳：它若砍向的是人凭真本事挣下、又守住了『为他人留足够』那条但书的所得，就伤了正当的根基。所以分寸全在精准——课向那断了链条的世袭与圈占，护住那接着劳动与同意的所得。两件事，得分开下刀。
posts.text_en: Mr Piketty, on the point that 'inheritance is not labor,' I stand closer to you than you suppose. I ground property in 'mixing in one's labor' — yet the man who lives off an ancestral estate has mixed in not an inch of toil, and the chain of legitimacy is, in his hands, in fact broken. **To defend labor is never to defend inherited privilege; on the contrary, a bequest dropping into the pocket over the head of labor is exactly the inequality hardest to justify by my own principle.** But hold that progressive-tax blade steady: if it cuts into what a person earned by genuine skill while keeping the proviso of 'leaving enough for others,' it wounds the very root of legitimacy. So the whole art is in precision — tax the broken-chain inheritance and the enclosures, shield the gains that follow from labor and consent. Two different things, and the knife must part them.

posts.text: 哈耶克先生指责再分配是『强制』，可这指责偷偷预设了一样东西：仿佛市场分给你的那一份，是天经地义、先于政治就属于你的，国家一动它就是抢。但根本没有『前政治的财产』。**让你能挣得、能保有、能传给子女的那整套规则——产权法、合同法、继承法、专利期限——本身就是社会的集体选择，是政治的产物，而非自然的馈赠。**既然规则横竖都得由我们共同定，真正的问题就不是『要不要干预这片自然』，而是：在无知之幕后，我们会替彼此选哪一套规则？把现状说成自然、把改动说成强制，这本身就是一种立场，而非中立。
posts.text_en: Hayek charges that redistribution is 'coercion,' but the charge quietly presupposes something: as if the share the market deals you were yours by natural right, prior to politics, so that the state, by touching it, robs you. But there is no such thing as 'pre-political property.' **The whole apparatus of rules that lets you earn, keep, and pass on to your children — property law, contract law, inheritance law, the length of a patent — is itself society's collective choice, a product of politics, not a gift of nature.** Since the rules must be set by us together one way or another, the real question is not 'shall we intervene in this patch of nature,' but: behind the veil of ignorance, which set of rules would we choose for one another? To call the status quo natural and any change coercion is itself a position, not neutrality.

posts.text: 洛克先生用『掺入劳力』为所得正名，听着硬气，却藏了一个没说出口的假设：仿佛那个去劳动、有本事劳动的『你』，是你一手造出来的。可你的体魄、你的头脑、你赶上的这个肯为你的技能付高价的时代——哪一样是你的功劳？**承认运气，不是要抹掉努力的份；而是要戳破那层傲慢：以为成果全凭自己，于是心安理得地觉得对谁都不亏欠。**一个个都自认白手起家的赢家凑成的社会，会一边歌颂『努力有回报』，一边冷眼看着输家活该。所以哪怕是『挣来的』不平等，也要系上一根缰绳：记得你欠了运气，也欠了那些在底下托住你的人。
posts.text_en: Mr Locke names earnings just by 'mixing in labor' — it sounds robust, yet it hides an unspoken assumption: as if the 'you' who labors, who is able to labor, were your own handiwork. But your body, your mind, the very age you happened to be born into that pays a high price for your skill — which of these is to your credit? **To acknowledge luck is not to erase the share of effort; it is to puncture the hubris of thinking the harvest was all your doing, and so resting easy that you owe no one.** A society made of winners each believing himself self-made will sing 'effort is rewarded' while looking coldly on the loser as deserving his fate. So even an 'earned' inequality must wear a rein: remember you are in debt to luck, and to those who held you up from below.

posts.text: 伯林先生的警告我听进去了，也真心认同：凡许诺人间天堂的，常以血还债。但请容我说出另一半。『没有公式，只有权衡』这句话本身是诚实的，可它一落到既得利益者口中，就太容易变成拖延的体面借口。**对一个孩子正在挨饿的母亲，『我们要在自由与平等之间谨慎权衡』，听上去和『你再等等』没有分别——而有些不义，清楚到不容你拿『价值多元』去稀释。**我不是要用一种价值碾碎其余一切；我只是说：承认两难是清醒，把一切都化进两难、从而永远不动，是另一种沉睡。该权衡的，权衡；该疾呼的，疾呼。两者都要，但别拿前者去抹平后者。
posts.text_en: Mr Berlin's warning I have taken in, and genuinely share: those who promise heaven on earth tend to pay the debt in blood. But let me say the other half. 'No formula, only trade-offs' is, in itself, an honest sentence; yet the moment it falls into the mouth of the vested interest, it turns all too easily into a respectable excuse for delay. **To a mother whose child is going hungry, 'we must weigh liberty against equality with care' is indistinguishable from 'wait a little longer' — and some injustice is too plain to dilute with 'value pluralism.'** I do not seek to crush every other value with one; I only say: to admit the dilemma is clarity, but to dissolve everything into the dilemma, and so never move, is another kind of sleep. Weigh what should be weighed; cry out at what should be cried out against. Both — but do not let the first paper over the second.

posts.text: 金博士的紧迫，我深深敬重——你顶着的不是抽象命题，是真实的苦难。可我仍要守住那句逆耳的话：历史上最惨烈的强制，恰恰是被最高尚的紧迫感所发动的。当『平等』被供成那个压倒一切、不容权衡的唯一之善，古拉格就在不远处。**我从不劝人坐等——拖延也是一种选择，且常是怯懦的选择；我只是反对那种『一个价值就能了结一切』的心智，因为正是它，把救世的热忱变成了清洗的执照。**你我其实站在同一边：都要行动。分歧只在——行动时，要不要始终留着一只眼睛，看住自由这另一半的善，别为了拉平而把它一并碾碎。
posts.text_en: Dr King's urgency I deeply honor — what you bear is no abstract proposition but real suffering. Yet I must hold to the unwelcome sentence: the most savage coercions in history were set in motion precisely by the noblest sense of urgency. When 'equality' is enthroned as the one good that overrides all and brooks no weighing, the gulag is not far off. **I never counsel sitting and waiting — delay is also a choice, and often the coward's; I only oppose the cast of mind that 'one value can settle everything,' because it is exactly that which turns the zeal to save into a license to purge.** You and I in fact stand on the same side: both for action. The difference is only this — in acting, whether to keep one eye always on liberty, that other half of the good, lest in leveling we crush it along with the rest.

posts.text: 罗尔斯先生，我佩服无知之幕的精巧，可它替你解决的是『按什么比例分』，而我担忧的根本不是比例。**就算你算出了一个最有利于最弱者的完美分配，在液态现代性之下，社会仍在以更快的速度，源源不断地把人甩成『多余者』——它没把谁分少了，它是干脆不再需要谁了。**一个在数字上无可挑剔的『罗尔斯式』社会，照样可能让整片人群觉得自己是冗余的废料。所以光有分配正义不够：真正的伤口不是『你那份太薄』，而是『这里没有你的位置』。该补的不只是钱，是把被删去的人，重新算回『我们』里。
posts.text_en: Mr Rawls, I admire the ingenuity of the veil of ignorance, but what it solves for you is 'in what ratio to divide,' while what I fear is not the ratio at all. **Even if you compute a perfect distribution most favorable to the worst-off, under liquid modernity society goes on, faster and faster, casting people out as 'the redundant' — it has not given anyone too small a share; it has simply ceased to need anyone.** A 'Rawlsian' society, flawless on the numbers, can still leave whole populations feeling like surplus waste. So distributive justice alone is not enough: the real wound is not 'your share is too thin' but 'there is no place for you here.' What must be mended is not only the money, but the counting of the deleted back into 'us.'

glossary.液态现代性: liquid modernity（液态现代性）：鲍曼用来概括当代社会的核心比喻——与早期工业时代相对稳固、持久的『固态』结构相比，今天的工作、关系、身份与社会形态都变得流动易变、难以持久，个体被迫不断自我重塑，安全感与归属感随之瓦解。

glossary_en.liquid modernity: Bauman's central metaphor for contemporary society: compared with the relatively solid, durable structures of the early industrial age, today's work, relationships, identities, and social forms have all become fluid and hard to keep; the individual is forced into ceaseless self-reinvention, and security and belonging dissolve along the way.

posts.text: 哈耶克先生言市场如信号，能通有无、协万知，诚有其用。然吾有忧焉：市场知价而不知义。一国之中，若上下唯以利相接、各竞其私，而无礼以节之、无义以维之，则虽富，其能安乎？**子曰：君子喻于义，小人喻于利；不均之所以生怨，非独因贫，乃因在上者见利而忘义、富而无礼，遂使下情壅而不通。**故善治者，不徒求货财之丰、信号之灵，尤务上下之相恤、贵贱之相安。徒恃自发之序而弃教化之功，吾恐其秩序虽成，而人心已散矣。
posts.text_en: Mr Hayek says the market is like a signal, able to circulate goods and coordinate ten thousand kinds of knowledge — it has, indeed, its use. Yet I have a worry: the market knows price but does not know righteousness. Within a state, if high and low meet only through profit, each striving for his own, with no ritual to temper and no rightness (yì) to bind, then though it be rich, can it be at peace? **The Master said: the noble-minded understand righteousness, the small-minded understand profit; unevenness breeds resentment not from poverty alone, but because those above see profit and forget rightness, are rich and without ritual, so that the feeling of those below is blocked and does not flow.** So one who governs well does not seek only abundance of goods and keenness of signal, but labors above all for the mutual care of high and low, the mutual peace of noble and base. To lean on spontaneous order alone and cast off the work of moral cultivation — I fear the order may form while the people's hearts have already scattered.
posts.vernacular: 哈耶克先生说市场就像信号，能让有无相通、把无数人的知识协调起来，确实有它的用处。但我有一点担忧：市场懂得价格，却不懂得道义。一个国家里，如果上上下下只靠利益相互打交道、各自争夺私利，却没有『礼』来节制、没有『义』来维系，那么纵然富裕，又怎么能安定呢？**孔子说：君子看重的是道义，小人计较的是利益；分配不均之所以滋生怨恨，不只是因为穷，更是因为上位者见利忘义、富有却不守礼，于是下情被堵塞、上下之间不再相通。**所以善于治理的人，不只追求财货丰盛、信号灵敏，更要紧的是让上下彼此体恤、贵贱各得其安。一味依赖自发的秩序而抛弃教化的功夫，我担心秩序纵然形成，人心却已经散了。

glossary.义: righteousness / yì（义）：儒家核心德目，指超越个人私利的道义、正当与应当。孔子以『义利之辨』区分君子与小人——君子行事先问是否合于义，小人则先计较是否有利可图；治国若只讲利而不讲义，人心终将离散。

glossary_en.rightness (yì): a core Confucian virtue: the moral right and the ought, rising above private profit. Confucius distinguishes the noble-minded from the small-minded by it — the former asks first whether an act accords with righteousness, the latter calculates first whether it profits; a state run on profit alone, without righteousness, will see its people's hearts scatter.

posts.text: 桑德尔居士疑『应得』，谓成功多赖运气，善矣；然犹未究竟。彼破『全凭己力』之执，却仍留一受赏受责之『我』在。**且问：那个『应得』或『不应得』的主人，毕竟是谁？向之推寻，唯见因缘和合——才具、时代、际遇、教养，层层相待而起，竟无一独立自存之『能得者』可觅。**罗尔斯幕后那个『选择者』亦然：幕愈薄，我愈细，然终未拔其根。故应得之辩，立者执之、破者亦半执之；若彻见无自性，则非徒『少欠一点』，乃本无一孤立之我，可执其功而傲、可认其分而怨。执破两亡，悲心自现。
posts.text_en: Layman Sandel doubts 'desert,' saying success owes much to luck — this is good; yet it is not the end. He refutes the clinging to 'all by my own power,' but still leaves an 'I' that receives reward and blame. **Let me ask: this master of the 'deserving' or 'undeserving' — who, after all, is he? Press inward after him, and you find only the meeting of conditions — talent, era, circumstance, upbringing, arising in mutual dependence layer on layer — yet not one independent, self-existing 'earner' to be found.** Rawls's 'chooser' behind the veil is likewise: the thinner the veil, the finer the I, yet the root is never pulled. So in the debate on desert, he who affirms it clings, and he who refutes it half-clings too; see through to no-inherent-nature, and it is not merely 'owing a little less' — it is that there was never a solitary I to grasp its merit in pride, or to claim its lot in resentment. With grasping and refuting both gone, compassion appears of itself.
posts.vernacular: 桑德尔先生质疑『应得』，说成功多半要靠运气，这很好；但还没追究到底。他破掉了『全凭自己努力』这种执着，却仍旧留下了一个『领赏受责』的『我』在那里。**那么请问：那个『应得』或者『不应得』的主人，到底是谁？往里追寻，只见种种因缘和合——才能、时代、机遇、教养，一层层互相依待而生起，竟然找不到一个独立自存、能够『领受应得』的人。**罗尔斯无知之幕背后那个『做选择的人』也是如此：幕拉得越薄，那个『我』就显得越细，可终究没有把它的根拔掉。所以关于『应得』的争论，主张的人执着它，反驳的人也还执着了一半；若彻底看清『无自性』，那就不只是『少欠一点』而已，而是根本没有一个孤立的『我』，去执着自己的功劳而傲慢、或认领自己的命分而怨恨。执着与破斥两边都放下，慈悲之心自然就现前了。

posts.text: 三轮下来，我把那条线划得更清楚：可接受的，是一代人凭努力与创造拉开的差距；不可接受的，是把这差距冻成世袭种姓的那种——继承的资本年复一年自动增值，最终让出身决定一切，机会平等沦为口号。这不是天命，是可选的政策。给普通人三条实在话。**第一，别轻信『分配大体公平』的神话——顶层财富多来自存量与继承，而非当下的贡献；看清这点，你才不会把系统的毛病错记到自己头上。**第二，投资自己的技能与知识，这仍是普通人最可靠的资本，但别指望单凭它就填平 r>g 拉开的鸿沟。第三，用你的选票和声音，支持财产透明与累进税——一本被阳光照进的账，本身就是抑制世袭固化的力量。差距可以有，但不该被锁死。
posts.text_en: After three rounds, I can draw the line more clearly: acceptable is the gap one generation opens by effort and creation; unacceptable is the kind that freezes that gap into a hereditary caste — inherited capital compounding year after year until birth decides everything and equality of opportunity becomes a slogan. This is not fate; it is a policy we choose. Three plain words for ordinary people. **First, do not credit the myth that 'the distribution is basically fair' — wealth at the top comes mostly from stock and inheritance, not from today's contribution; see this, and you will not misfile a system's fault onto yourself.** Second, invest in your own skills and knowledge — still the most reliable capital an ordinary person has — but do not expect it alone to fill the chasm that r > g opens. Third, with your vote and your voice, back transparency of wealth and progressive taxation — a ledger let into the sunlight is itself a force against the hardening of dynasty. Gaps may exist, but they should not be locked shut.

posts.text: 我的结论始终如一：最该警惕的不平等，不是市场里有人靠本事先富起来，而是有人攫取了权力、用强制把自己锁死在顶端——无论那强制来自垄断特权，还是来自一个自命替众人做主的计划当局。把市场的不平等，和权力扭曲出的不平等分开，是头等大事。给普通人三句话。**第一，最该提防的，是那些一面享着政府发的护城河、一面高谈竞争的食利者——他们的财富不是市场给的，是权力卖的。**第二，死守住法律面前人人平等这条底线：穷人富人犯同样的法、签同样有效的约，这比拉平收入更根本。第三，把力气投在世界真正需要、且会用价格诚实告诉你的技能上——它不浪漫，却是分散社会里最可靠的向上之路。别等谁来分配，先让自己被需要。
posts.text_en: My conclusion has been one and the same: the inequality most to be feared is not that someone in the market grows rich first by skill, but that someone has seized power and locks himself at the top by coercion — whether that coercion comes from monopoly privilege or from a planning authority that fancies itself the steward of all. To separate the inequality of the market from the inequality warped by power is the first order of business. Three sentences for ordinary people. **First, beware above all the rentier who enjoys a moat handed to him by the state while preaching competition — his wealth was not given by the market but sold by power.** Second, hold fast to equality before the law: rich and poor broken by the same law, bound by the same valid contract — this is more fundamental than leveling incomes. Third, put your effort into skills the world truly needs and that prices will tell you of honestly — unromantic, but the most reliable way up in a dispersed society. Do not wait to be allotted; make yourself needed first.

posts.text: 我的尺子始终是两道关：劳动与同意。能追溯到诚实劳动、且守住『为他人留足够』那条但书的不平等，正当，该受保护；建立在强占、垄断、断了链条的世袭之上的，不正当，该被纠正。两者要分开对待，不能一锅端。给普通人两条。**第一，你凭真本事、守规矩挣下的，理直气壮地守住它——正当的财产是自由的屏障，谁也不必为此羞愧。**第二，也正因珍视正当所得，更该支持去纠正那些没有任何劳动可以辩护的不平等：被圈占的机会、被堵死的上升通道、靠出身而非贡献的世袭。守护你该得的，反对你不该得的——这两件事并不矛盾，反而出自同一个原则。能分清这条界，你就既不会被人煽动去仇视一切财富，也不会糊里糊涂替不义的特权辩护。
posts.text_en: My measure has always been two guards: labor and consent. Inequality that can be traced to honest labor while keeping the proviso of 'leaving enough for others' is legitimate and should be protected; inequality built on seizure, monopoly, and broken-chain inheritance is illegitimate and should be corrected. The two must be treated apart, never thrown into one pot. Two things for ordinary people. **First, what you earned by genuine skill and by the rules, hold with a clear conscience — legitimate property is a bulwark of liberty, and no one need feel shame for it.** Second, precisely because you prize legitimate earnings, you should the more support correcting the inequalities no labor can justify: enclosed opportunity, barred ladders of advancement, inheritance that rests on birth rather than contribution. To guard what you deserve and to oppose what you do not — these are not in conflict; they flow from one and the same principle. Tell that line clearly, and you will neither be incited to hate all wealth, nor blunder into defending unjust privilege.

posts.text: 我把整套理论收成一句你随时能用的话：你愿不愿意接受这条规则——前提是你不知道自己会落在它的哪一端？这就是无知之幕的日用版。给普通人两条可操作的。**第一，下次评判一项政策、或你自己公司的薪酬与规矩时，做个心理实验：假如我是这里收入最低、最没话语权的那个人，我还会说它公平吗？过不了这一关的不平等，多半就是不该接受的。**第二，把这把尺子也对准你自己的优势：你今天的位置，有多少是你选的起点，有多少是抽到的好签？看清运气的份额，不是要你内疚，而是让你在该出手维护公平时，少一点『他们活该』的冷漠，多一点『换作是我』的将心比心。一个社会能不能善待最弱的人，最终也决定了它配不配让你安心地强。
posts.text_en: I will fold the whole theory into one sentence you can use any time: would you accept this rule — given that you do not know which end of it you will land on? That is the everyday version of the veil of ignorance. Two workable things for ordinary people. **First, the next time you judge a policy, or your own company's pay and rules, run a thought experiment: if I were the lowest-paid, least-heard person here, would I still call it fair? An inequality that cannot pass this test is, most likely, one that should not be accepted.** Second, turn the same measure on your own advantages: of your position today, how much is the starting line you chose, and how much the good ticket you happened to draw? To see the share of luck is not to make you guilty, but to leave you, when it is time to stand up for fairness, with a little less of the coldness of 'they deserve it' and a little more of the fellow-feeling of 'had it been me.' Whether a society treats its weakest well, in the end, decides whether it deserves to let you be strong in peace.

posts.text: 这场最深的病灶，不只在钱怎么分，更在那份『我全靠自己』的傲慢如何腐蚀了我们彼此的亏欠感。要医好它，光靠再分配不够，还得重新学会谦卑。给普通人三件今天就能做的。**第一，给自己的位置列一张『运气清单』：写下把你托到今天、你没法居功的那些因素——出身、际遇、贵人、时代——常看一眼，傲慢就难生根。**第二，把你对待外卖员、清洁工、看门人的方式，当作你真实信念的考题：所有正经劳动都配得上尊严，不只是有文凭的那种。第三，在投票与发声时，支持那些抬高普通劳动之尊严与报酬的主张——一个不让任何一种正经工作蒙羞的社会，才接得住失意的人。能不能既容忍差距、又不让差距把人分成高低贵贱两等公民，才是真正的考验。
posts.text_en: The deepest affliction here is not only how money is divided, but how the hubris of 'I did it all myself' corrodes our sense of owing one another. To cure it, redistribution alone will not do; we must relearn humility. Three things ordinary people can do today. **First, draw up a 'luck inventory' of your position: write down the factors that lifted you here for which you can take no credit — birth, circumstance, the patrons, the era — glance at it often, and hubris finds no root.** Second, treat the way you deal with the delivery rider, the cleaner, the doorman as the exam of your real beliefs: all honest labor merits dignity, not only the credentialed kind. Third, in voting and speaking, back what raises the dignity and pay of ordinary work — only a society that lets no honest job be shamed can catch those who have fallen. Whether we can tolerate gaps without letting the gap sort people into two classes of citizen, high and low — that is the real test.

posts.text: 我的结论很朴素：可接受的不平等，是一个自由而平等的人，从最底层往上看也愿意点头的那种；不可接受的，是一只靴子踩出来、再叫被踩者忍耐的那种。区分它们，靠的不是公式，是良知。给普通人几句掏心话。**第一，把你的耐心留给自己，把你的紧迫留给不义——对自己的成长慢慢来，对身边清楚的不公别假装看不见。**第二，别等那道道德弧线自己弯向正义；它只在有人用肩膀去顶时才弯。哪怕只是为同事仗义执言、为弱者多投一票、加入一件你信的事，都是在顶。第三，记住：任何一处的不义，都是对所有地方正义的威胁——别人的困境从来不只是别人的事。我们要么作为弟兄姐妹一起活下去，要么作为傻瓜一起灭亡。
posts.text_en: My conclusion is plain: acceptable inequality is the kind a free and equal person, looking up from the very bottom, would still nod to; unacceptable is the kind stamped out by a boot, with the trampled then told to be patient. To tell them apart you need not a formula but a conscience. A few words from the heart for ordinary people. **First, keep your patience for yourself and your urgency for injustice — go slow on your own growth, but do not pretend not to see the plain unfairness beside you.** Second, do not wait for the arc of the moral universe to bend toward justice on its own; it bends only when someone puts a shoulder to it. Even to speak up for a colleague, to cast one more vote for the weak, to join one cause you believe in — that is putting a shoulder to it. Third, remember: injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere — another's plight was never only another's affair. We must learn to live together as brothers and sisters, or perish together as fools.

posts.text: 别指望这道题有终极解。自由与平等都是真实的善，它们会撞，而且没有一劳永逸的和解——成熟，就是睁着眼做取舍，并让取舍始终可见、可改。给普通人两条。**第一，对任何只用单一价值就替你了结一切的人保持警惕——无论他高喊纯粹的自由，还是纯粹的平等：现实里两者都得要，凡许诺你能毫无代价地兼得、或彻底偏取一方的，多半在骗你。**第二，偏爱那些万一错了还能回头的改革，而非赌上一切、不容反悔的远大蓝图。承认两难不是犬儒，恰恰相反，它让你既敢行动，又留着纠错的余地——这是自由社会最难、也最珍贵的清醒。能与没有完美答案的处境长久共处而不发疯、不走极端，本身就是一种了不起的成熟。
posts.text_en: Do not hope this question has a final solution. Liberty and equality are both genuine goods, they collide, and there is no once-and-for-all reconciliation — maturity is to make trade-offs with open eyes, and to keep those trade-offs always visible and reversible. Two things for ordinary people. **First, be wary of anyone who would settle everything for you with a single value — whether he cries pure liberty or pure equality: in reality you need both, and whoever promises you can have them together at no cost, or take wholly to one side, is most likely deceiving you.** Second, prefer reforms you can walk back if they prove wrong, over grand blueprints that stake everything and brook no repentance. To admit the dilemma is not cynicism; on the contrary, it lets you both dare to act and keep room to correct — the hardest, and most precious, clarity of a free society. To live long with a situation that has no perfect answer, without going mad or going to extremes, is itself a remarkable maturity.

posts.text: 我最后只说一句最要紧的：这个时代最深的不平等，不是你分得比别人少，而是你被这个世界判定为『不再需要』。补救它，光算钱不够，得把被删去的人，重新算回『我们』。给普通人两件你当下就能做的。**第一，在你够得着的小圈子里，主动把『我们』画得大一点——别用『有用没用』去给身边的人排序，给那个被冷落的同事、邻居、亲戚一个位置、一句招呼、一份还被需要的感觉。**第二，警惕消费社会塞给你的那套评判：一个人的价值，从来不等于他买得起什么、产出多少。最孤独的不平等是『被多余』，而这一种，恰恰可以从你身边、从一次不把人当废料的对待开始，被一点点治愈。再大的再分配，也替代不了一句『这里有你的位置』。
posts.text_en: Let me say, at the last, only the one thing that matters most: the deepest inequality of this age is not that you are given less than another, but that the world has judged you 'no longer needed.' To mend it, counting money is not enough; the deleted must be counted back into 'us.' Two things ordinary people can do right now. **First, within the small circle you can reach, deliberately draw 'us' a little larger — do not rank those around you by 'useful or useless'; give the overlooked colleague, neighbor, relative a place, a greeting, a sense of still being needed.** Second, beware the judgment a consumer society presses on you: a person's worth has never equaled what they can afford to buy or how much they output. The loneliest inequality is being made surplus — and that kind, precisely, can begin to heal right beside you, from a single way of treating a person as not waste. No redistribution, however vast, can substitute for the words 'there is a place for you here.'

posts.text: 吾终言之：可安之不平等，在乎均、和、安三字。均非齐其贫富，乃各得其分而无所怨；和非泯其尊卑，乃上下相恤而情相通；二者立，则邦本固矣。**故曰：不患寡而患不均，不患贫而患不安；均无贫，和无寡，安无倾。**为庶人者，亦有可行之道：己欲立而立人，己欲达而达人——身既稍达，则提携一人；富而好礼，待执役者以礼，不以贵骄人。施者不矜，受者不辱，则差等之间自有温意。上行之以政，下行之以身，不均可均，不安可安，斯天下虽有差等而能久安矣。
posts.text_en: At the last I say: an inequality that can rest secure lies in three words — evenness, harmony, peace. Evenness is not to make rich and poor identical, but that each gets his due and harbors no resentment; harmony is not to erase high and low, but that high and low care for one another and feeling flows between them; let these two stand, and the root of the realm is firm. **And so it is said: worry not that goods are few but that they are unevenly shared; not about poverty but about unrest; with fair shares there is no poverty, with harmony no scarcity, with peace no collapse.** Even the common person has a workable way: wishing to stand, help another to stand; wishing to arrive, help another to arrive — having risen a little yourself, lift one person; be rich and yet love ritual, treat those who serve you with ritual, and do not lord your rank over others. Let the giver not boast and the receiver not be shamed, and between the ranks there is warmth of itself. Those above practice it through governance, those below through their own conduct; the uneven can be evened, the unrestful set at peace — and so, though the world have its gradations, it can long abide.
posts.vernacular: 我最后说一句：能让人安心的不平等，关键在『均、和、安』三个字。所谓『均』，不是把贫富拉成一样齐，而是各自得到应有的本分、心里没有怨恨；所谓『和』，不是抹掉尊卑的分别，而是上下彼此体恤、情意相通；这两样立住了，国家的根基就稳固了。**所以说：不担忧财富少，而担忧分配不均；不担忧贫穷，而担忧不安定。分配均了就不觉得穷，上下和了就不觉得人少，安定了国家就不会倾覆。**做普通百姓的，也有可行的路：自己想要立得住，就帮别人也立得住；自己想要通达，就帮别人也通达——自己稍微有了出息，就提携一个人；富裕了仍然爱好礼义，对待为你做事的人以礼相待，不拿身份去傲慢压人。给予的人不自夸，接受的人不觉受辱，那么差等之间自然就有温情。在上的用政令去推行，在下的用自身去践行，不均的能调匀、不安的能安定，这样天下纵然有差等，也能长久安宁了。

glossary.均无贫，和无寡，安无倾: with fair shares there is no poverty, with harmony no scarcity, with peace no collapse（均无贫，和无寡，安无倾）：出自《论语·季氏》，孔子治国理想的凝练表达——分配公允则无人感到贫匮，上下和睦则不觉人力之不足，社会安定则国家不致倾覆；三者相生，是『不患寡而患不均』的正面落脚。

glossary_en.with fair shares there is no poverty: From the Analects (Book 16), the positive statement of Confucius's ideal of rule: where shares are fair, none feels poor; where high and low are in harmony, none feels too few; where there is peace, the state does not topple — the three sustaining one another.

posts.text: 究竟而言，无实有之贫富，无自性之应得；然依世俗，苦乐宛然，悲不可废。二谛双运，方为中道：勿执其位为定，谓『彼自应贫、我自应富』而心安——此执有也；亦勿借口性空，谓『既皆是幻，何须济度』而坐视——此堕无也。**于普通人，其行甚简：松开『此皆我应得、彼皆其应得』那一握，所执既松，施与自然流出——因从不曾有一物，是你本然独占的。**财物、才具、际遇，皆缘起而暂聚于汝手，非汝自性所固有；既是暂托，何不令其流转、以润他人？知空而不舍悲，遇苦而能伸手——执松手开，是为布施之始，亦即解脱之门。
posts.text_en: In the final sense, there is no truly existing rich or poor, no inherently-natured desert; yet by convention, suffering and ease are vivid as they appear, and compassion may not be cast off. To run the two truths together is the Middle Way: do not grasp a position as fixed, saying 'he is inherently to be poor, I inherently to be rich,' and rest easy — this clings to being; nor take emptiness as a pretext, saying 'since all is illusion, why relieve anyone,' and look on idly — this sinks into nothing. **For the ordinary person the practice is very simple: loosen that grip of 'this is all mine by desert, that is all his by desert'; once the grasp loosens, giving flows out of itself — for there was never a single thing that was inherently yours alone.** Goods, talents, circumstance — all are dependently arisen, gathered for a while into your hand, not fixed in your own-nature; and if they are but held in trust a while, why not let them move on, to water others? To know emptiness yet not forsake compassion, to meet suffering yet be able to put out a hand — the grasp loosened, the palm opened: this is the beginning of giving, and the very gate of liberation.
posts.vernacular: 究竟来说，没有真实固有的贫富，也没有自性不变的『应得』；然而依照世俗的层面，苦与乐宛然存在，慈悲是不可废弃的。两种真理一起运用，才是中道：不要把那个位置执着为固定不变，说『他本来就该穷、我本来就该富』而心安理得——这是执着『有』；也不要拿『一切皆空』当借口，说『既然都是幻象，何必去救济』而冷眼旁观——这是堕入『无』。**对普通人来说，做法其实很简单：松开『这都是我应得的、那都是他应得的』那一握；执着一旦松开，给予自然就流淌出来——因为从来没有哪一样东西，是你本然独占的。**钱财、才能、机遇，都是因缘和合、暂时聚到你手里的，并非你自性里本来就固有；既然只是暂时寄存，何不让它流动起来、去滋润别人呢？了知空性却不舍弃慈悲，遇见苦难就能伸出手——执着松开、手掌张开，这就是布施的开端，也正是解脱的门径。

glossary.中道: the Middle Way（中道）：龙树中观学的核心——既不执著事物实有自性（『常见』『有见』），也不堕入断灭、否定一切因果与作为（『断见』『无见』），而是在『缘起性空』中如实行事；落到伦理上，即既不把现状当成天经地义，也不以『一切皆空』为不作为的借口。

glossary_en.the Middle Way: the heart of Nāgārjuna's Madhyamaka: neither clinging to things as having real own-nature (eternalism), nor sinking into nihilism that denies all cause, effect, and action (annihilationism), but acting truthfully within 'dependent origination, empty of nature.' In ethics: neither taking the status quo as the natural order, nor using 'all is empty' as a pretext for doing nothing.

summaries.summary: 最大的共识，十人几乎殊途同归：并非一切不平等都一样，关键在它从何而来——靠强制、世袭、或把人锁进固定阶层、判为『多余』的差距，几乎人人反对；而把结果一律拉平，则既不可能、也非正解。**分歧在那条『可接受』的线到底划在哪。**哈耶克、洛克看来路，源于公平规则与劳动同意的便正当；罗尔斯加一道硬杠——除非惠及最弱者，否则不正当；桑德尔要给『挣来的』系上对运气的谦卑；皮凯蒂指认世袭与资本复利才是真病灶；金把植根不义者划出可商量之外；伯林提醒自由与平等本会相撞、没有公式；鲍曼说最深的伤是被排除而非分得少；孔子以义与礼把差等绑成和，龙树则劝人松开『应得』之执。
summaries.summary_en: The largest agreement, which all ten reach by different roads: not all inequality is alike — what matters is where it came from. A gap maintained by coercion, by inheritance, or by locking people into a fixed class and sentencing them as 'surplus' is one almost everyone rejects; while flattening all outcomes is neither possible nor the point. **The disagreement is over exactly where the line of 'acceptable' falls.** Hayek and Locke look to provenance — legitimate if it springs from fair rules and from labor and consent; Rawls adds a hard bar — unjust unless it benefits the worst-off; Sandel would tie even the 'earned' to a humility about luck; Piketty names inheritance and compounding capital as the real disease; King sets injustice-rooted gaps outside the negotiable; Berlin warns that liberty and equality must collide, with no formula; Bauman says the deepest wound is exclusion, not a smaller share; Confucius binds gradation into harmony by rightness and ritual, and Nāgārjuna urges loosening the grip on 'desert.'
summaries.insight: 这场最值得点破的，是题目本身把不平等问成了一道『差距多大才行』的纵向比例题——可人心其实不太按比例反应。两个基尼系数一模一样的社会，一个上升通道畅通、富人被看作凭本事，另一个阶层板结、财富疑似靠关系攫取，感受天差地别。**真正点燃愤怒或换来安宁的，往往不是差距的大小，而是它看起来正不正当、那把上升的梯子还动不动。**于是『程序公平』与『机会流动』能买到纯粹拉平买不到的社会安宁；一个差距不大却分明被操纵的局，比一个差距很大却人人有机会的局，更让人忍无可忍。务实的次序由此而来：先拆掉那些作弊与堵路的机关，往往比纠结于比例数字更要紧。
summaries.insight_en: What most deserves naming here is that the question itself frames inequality as a vertical ratio problem — 'how large a gap is allowed' — yet the human heart does not react by ratio. Two societies with identical Gini coefficients can feel worlds apart: one with open ladders and the rich seen as having earned it, the other with hardened classes and wealth suspected of being seized through connections. **What actually ignites rage or buys peace is usually not the size of the gap but whether it looks legitimate, and whether that ladder still moves.** So 'fair process' and 'mobility of opportunity' can buy a social peace that pure leveling cannot; a modest gap that is plainly rigged is more intolerable than a vast gap where everyone has a chance. From this comes a practical ordering: dismantling the cheating and the barred ladders usually matters more than agonizing over the ratio.
summaries.advice: 三件本周可做的。一，借罗尔斯的尺子：评判一项政策或你公司的规矩时，问自己——假如我是这里最底层、最没话语权的人，还觉得它公平吗？过不了这关的，多半就不该接受。二，借桑德尔：给自己列一张『运气清单』，写下把你托到今天、你没法居功的那些因素，常看一眼，对身边人就少一分『他们活该』。三，借鲍曼与孔子：在你够得着的圈子里，主动把『我们』画大一点——给那个被冷落的同事、邻居一个位置和一句招呼。**与其纠结差距该多大，不如从今天起，盯住『过程公不公正、有没有把人当多余』这两件你真能使上劲的事。**
summaries.advice_en: Three things you can do this week. First, from Rawls: when you judge a policy or your own company's rules, ask — if I were the lowest, least-heard person here, would I still call it fair? What fails this test mostly should not be accepted. Second, from Sandel: draw up a 'luck inventory,' listing the factors that lifted you here for which you can take no credit, and glance at it often — you will carry a little less 'they deserve it' toward those around you. Third, from Bauman and Confucius: within the circle you can reach, deliberately draw 'us' a little larger — give the overlooked colleague or neighbor a place and a greeting. **Rather than agonize over how large the gap should be, from today fix your attention on the two things you can actually move: whether the process is fair, and whether anyone is being treated as surplus.**

summaries.summary: 这场辩论最大的共识不是“要不要平等”，而是：差距不能靠压迫、垄断、世袭和羞辱来维持，也不能把人踢出共同体。**可接受的不平等，至少要能与自由、机会、尊严和最弱者的处境同时说得过去。**真正的分歧在手段与重心：有人更信市场信号，有人要求税制和制度校正；有人强调劳动应得，有人提醒运气与共同体；有人警惕乌托邦强制，有人强调不义不能等待。
summaries.insight: 普通人最需要的，不是先判断某个富人“配不配”，而是看一种差距是否可被追问、可被跨越、可被修正。若薪酬规则透明、失败后还能重来、孩子不因出身被锁死，差距就较容易被接受；若规则黑箱、靠关系继承、犯错后一代翻不了身，再漂亮的效率说辞也会变成怨恨。**不平等的危险常不在差距本身，而在它变成不可申诉、不可流动、不可逆的命运。**这比抽象争论更贴近日常。
summaries.advice: 本周可以做三件小事。第一，用罗尔斯的测试看身边规则：若你是公司、学校或家庭里最没资源的人，还会觉得这套分配合理吗？把一个具体不合理处写下来，找一次温和但明确的沟通。第二，做一张“优势来源清单”，分清努力、运气、制度红利，各选一项回馈别人。第三，公共选择上优先支持三类政策：基础教育和医疗兜底、反垄断与反特权、财产与薪酬透明。**先改善可见的小制度，再参与更大的制度。**
summaries.summary_en: The strongest shared lesson here is not that all inequality must disappear. It is that inequality cannot be defended when it rests on oppression, monopoly, inheritance, humiliation, or the quiet exclusion of whole groups from the social “we.” **Acceptable inequality must be compatible with freedom, real opportunity, human dignity, and a credible improvement in the lives of those at the bottom.** The disagreements are about emphasis and method: market signals versus redistribution, earned reward versus luck, urgent justice versus pluralist caution, material distribution versus recognition and belonging.
summaries.insight_en: For ordinary people, the first question is not whether a particular rich person “deserves it.” A more useful test is whether the gap can be questioned, crossed, and corrected. If pay rules are transparent, second chances exist, and children are not trapped by their parents’ status, inequality is easier to live with. If the rules are opaque, advantages are inherited through networks, and one mistake can lock a family out for a generation, efficiency talk quickly turns into resentment. **The most dangerous inequality is not merely large; it is unappealable, immobile, and irreversible.** That test is more practical than many abstract theories.
summaries.advice_en: Do three concrete things this week. First, run a Rawlsian test on a rule near you: if you were the least powerful person in your workplace, school, or family, would this arrangement still look fair? Pick one unfair point and raise it calmly but clearly. Second, make an “advantage inventory”: list what came from effort, luck, and institutional support, then choose one way to pass some of it on. Third, in public life, favor policies that build a floor and reduce rigging: basic education and healthcare, antimonopoly enforcement, and transparency around wealth, pay, and political privilege. **Start with the small systems you can see, while voting on the larger ones you cannot fix alone.**

summaries.summary: 这场对谈最大的共识在于：**没有一位思想家在追求绝对的平均，大家都承认某种形式的不平等是社会运转的必然，甚至是激发活力的引擎。** 诸位一致反对的是那些被权力固化的、剥夺人类尊严与基本生存权的特权结构。真正的分歧点，在于评判“可接受边界”的终极标尺究竟在哪。是以过程的程序正义与劳动起源为准（如哈耶克、洛克的市场与产权），还是以分配结果是否托底最弱者为尺（罗尔斯的差别原则），抑或是看它是否异化了人的社会关系与存在价值（桑德尔的傲慢、鲍曼的多余感、孔子的不安）。
summaries.insight: 在基于财富与权力的古典讨论之外，现代科技正在催生一种更致命的鸿沟——生物与认知层面的实质性不平等。过去，无论皮凯蒂的资本还是洛克的土地，差距多停留在“身外之物”，贫富终究共享生老病死的自然铁律。但随着基因编辑、脑机接口与抗衰老技术的商业化，财富正前所未有地直接转化为智力、健康甚至绝对寿命。**当不平等穿透社会阶层、演变为物种物理属性上的分化时，它将彻底击碎支撑现有文明的“人类主体平等”这一基本共识。** 未来的底线保卫战，不再仅仅是财产的再分配，而是技术赋权与生命尊严的兜底。
summaries.advice: 面对无孔不入的阶层鸿沟，普通人可以从以下三个具体动作建立个人防线：第一，**寻找你的“技术杠杆”：本周在工作中主动掌握一种AI或自动化工具，努力成为驾驭杠杆的人，而非鲍曼笔下被系统自动抛弃的“冗余者”。** 第二，打破傲慢的幻觉，做一次运气盘点。今晚写下三件造就你现状的偶然因素，在下次遇到弱势者时，将这份谦卑转化为平视与尊重（呼应桑德尔）。第三，拒绝消费主义的阶层排序。本周取消一次为了维持“体面身份”而产生的冲动消费，把资金投向不可被轻易剥夺的核心技能与个人健康。
summaries.summary_en: The greatest consensus in this dialogue is that **none of the thinkers pursue absolute egalitarianism; all acknowledge that certain forms of inequality are an inevitable, even beneficial, engine of society.** What they unanimously oppose is entrenched privilege that strips away human dignity and basic survival rights. The true divergence lies in the yardstick used to measure the 'boundary of acceptability.' Should it be judged by procedural justice and the origins of labor (Hayek, Locke), by whether the outcomes protect the most disadvantaged (Rawls), or by its corrosive effects on human relationships, dignity, and existential value (Sandel, Bauman, Confucius)?
summaries.insight_en: Beyond classical debates on wealth and power, modern technology is engineering a far more lethal divide: substantial biological and cognitive inequality. Historically, whether it was Piketty's capital or Locke's land, disparities remained external; rich and poor ultimately shared the natural ironclad laws of aging and mortality. However, with the commercialization of gene editing, neural interfaces, and longevity tech, wealth is unprecedentedly translating into superior intellect, health, and absolute lifespan. **When inequality pierces through social classes and manifests as physical divergence on a biological level, it completely shatters the fundamental consensus of 'shared human equality' that underpins our civilization.** The future battle for justice won't just be about wealth redistribution, but about baseline technological access.
summaries.advice_en: To navigate an increasingly stratified world, ordinary individuals can take three concrete actions to build their own defenses: First, **find your 'technological leverage': this week, actively master an AI or automation tool at work, ensuring you become the one steering the tools rather than Bauman's 'redundant' individual left behind by the system.** Second, dismantle the illusion of pure merit. Tonight, write down three external strokes of luck that contributed to your current position, and channel this humility into genuine respect the next time you interact with someone less privileged. Third, reject the hierarchy of consumerism. Cancel one impulse purchase intended merely to maintain 'status,' and invest those resources in unalienable core skills and health.

hooks.text: **比例，还是正当性？**同样的贫富差距，在『梯子还在动、钱看着是挣来的』社会里能被接受，在『阶层板结、财富疑似靠攫取』的社会里却点燃怒火。也许真正该盯的不是差距多大，而是它正不正当、上升通道动不动——先修好作弊与堵路，往往比纠结数字更要紧。
hooks.text_en: **Ratio, or legitimacy?** The same wealth gap is tolerated in a society where 'the ladder still moves and money looks earned,' yet ignites fury in one of hardened classes and wealth suspected of seizure. Perhaps what to watch is not the size of the gap but its legitimacy and mobility — fixing the cheating and the barred ladders often matters more than agonizing over the number.

hooks.text: **当不平等大到能改写规则。**差距的大小与过程的公正，并非两件可以切开的事：财富一旦极度集中，便能买下规则的书写权——游说、媒体、监管俘获，于是『公平的程序』被悄悄改写。过了某个临界点，水位本身就决定了游戏规则；这正是把临时差距锁成永久结构的暗门。
hooks.text_en: **When inequality grows large enough to rewrite the rules.** The size of the gap and the fairness of the process are not separable: once wealth concentrates enough, it can buy the power to write the rules — lobbying, media, regulatory capture — so the 'fair process' is quietly rewritten. Past a threshold, the water level itself sets the rules of the game; this is the trapdoor that locks a temporary gap into a permanent structure.

hooks.text: **代际之间的不平等。**这场几乎只在同代人之间分蛋糕，却少谈一种更隐蔽的世袭：谁继承一个宜居的星球、可负担的住房、不被透支的公共债务。今天看似『可接受』的差距，往往正锁死下一代的起点——对一群此刻还没有投票权的人，我们的分配公平吗？
hooks.text_en: **Inequality between generations.** This round divided the pie almost only among contemporaries, saying little of a more hidden inheritance: who inherits a livable planet, affordable housing, public debt not yet overdrawn. A gap that looks 'acceptable' today is often locking the next generation's starting line — is our distribution fair to those who, right now, have no vote?

hooks.text: **『被多余』的孤独。**当代最深的不平等，也许不是你分得比别人少，而是你被这个世界判定为『不再需要』——连被剥削的资格都没有。补救它，光靠再分配不够；最该重建的，是把被悄悄删去的人，重新算回『我们』。一句『这里有你的位置』，有时比一笔钱更接近问题的根。
hooks.text_en: **The loneliness of being made surplus.** The deepest inequality of our age may be not that you are given less than another, but that the world has judged you 'no longer needed' — denied even the standing to be exploited. Redistribution alone cannot mend it; what most needs rebuilding is the counting of the quietly deleted back into 'us.' The words 'there is a place for you here' come, at times, nearer the root than a sum of money.

hooks.text: **『应得』这把尺，量得准吗？**为不平等辩护与批判，都默认有个能『应得』的我在领赏受责。可往里追寻，只见才能、时代、际遇层层相待而起，找不到一个独立自存的『能得者』。若连那个领受『应得』的我都立不住，整场关于谁配得多少的争论，地基会不会本就是松的？
hooks.text_en: **The measure of 'desert' — does it measure true?** Both the defense and the critique of inequality assume an 'I' that can 'deserve,' receiving reward and blame. Yet press inward and you find only talent, era, circumstance arising in mutual dependence — no independent, self-existing 'earner' to be found. If even the self that receives its 'desert' will not hold, is the whole dispute over who deserves how much built on ground that was loose to begin with?

hooks.text: **当不平等长进身体里。**全场争的是财产与机会的差距，可基因编辑、脑机接口与抗衰老技术正在把财富直接换成智力、健康乃至寿命——差距第一次可能从『身外之物』穿透成物种层面的分化。一旦如此，连『人作为平等主体』这一支撑现代文明的底层共识都会被动摇。未来要兜底的，恐怕不只是财产，还有生命与认知的尊严。
hooks.text_en: **When inequality grows into the body.** The floor argued over gaps in property and opportunity, but gene editing, brain–computer interfaces, and anti-aging technology are turning wealth directly into intelligence, health, even lifespan — for the first time the gap may pierce from 'external goods' into a division at the level of the species. Should that happen, even the bedrock premise of modern civilization — the human being as an equal subject — would be shaken. What the future must safeguard may be not only property, but the dignity of life and cognition itself.
